input.rationale: The account now has its bound, so the next judgment-changing question is whether the per-message repair survives a repeating sender: the mechanism is only a one-heartbeat disruption if the attacker has to stop, and a sustained defeat of the lease if the same message can be re-delivered each round. I register that as a child question and request one new fixed experiment (fourth test function, its own p_ prefixed stream) that runs the already-executed scenario three times in a row, repairing the follower with the leader's real heartbeat each round and re-delivering the same peer-form MsgForgetLeader before the same retried pre-vote request. The harness runs natively with the predicted events: round 0 without the forgery gives no grant, and every subsequent round restores the leader context, loses it again, and grants. The formal reading is deferred to the receipt.

investigations.question: Does a peer that re-delivers the same MsgForgetLeader once per heartbeat round keep a follower from enforcing its leader lease while the leader is healthy, so that the identical up-to-date candidate's pre-vote is granted on every attempt rather than during a single heartbeat interval?
investigations.hypothesis: Each round follows the same path: the leader's real heartbeat restores r.lead (=1), the accepted peer-form MsgForgetLeader clears it again (=0), and with lead==None the CheckQuorum lease test fails, so the up-to-date candidate's pre-vote is granted every round; the repair path is genuinely working (lead returns to 1 each round) but is defeated by the attacker's cadence rather than being broken.
investigations.discriminator: Round 0 without any forgery (control: no grant), then rounds 1-3 each delivering the leader's real heartbeat, the same forged message and the same retried pre-vote. A single grant would bound the effect to one window; grants in every round while the leader keeps beating and stays leader show that the window can be kept open indefinitely by the sender.

scope.description: Fourth test function in the same harness file: a real three-voter group elected for node 1, a real pre-vote request produced by a real campaign on node 3 and retried unchanged, and a loop of three rounds in which the leader is ticked, its real heartbeat is delivered to follower 2, the peer-form MsgForgetLeader (From=3, To=2, no term field) is delivered through RawNode.Step, and the retried pre-vote is delivered again.
assumptions: A peer may deliver an arbitrary protobuf message type to the public inbound path RawNode.Step, repeatedly and at will.
Ticks are the target's logical clock; only the leader is ticked, so follower election timeouts never fire and the leader stays healthy throughout.
The candidate's request is reused unchanged across rounds, representing a retry by a candidate that is still waiting; the follower stays at term 2 because a pre-vote never changes the term.
All nodes start from equal storage snapshots (index=10, term=1, voters {1,2,3}).
excluded: Wall-clock timing and multi-host transport behaviour.
Whether a real candidate would keep retrying after its first grant is taken (the grant is fed nowhere here).

experiment.prefix: Elect node 1 for real, deliver its real heartbeat to follower 2, emit the pre-vote control round, then repeat three rounds: leader tick (one heartbeat), deliver the real heartbeat to follower 2, deliver the peer-form MsgForgetLeader, deliver the unchanged retried pre-vote. Each round emits the heartbeat's lead transition, the accepted message with its lead transition, and the pre-vote outcome (whether a MsgPreVoteResp was produced and whether it rejected).
experiment.responsibility: The raft module owns the lease rule that keeps a follower from supporting a candidate while it hears from a live leader, and owns which message types are acceptable from the network.

comparisons.description: Control: in the round without any forged message the retried pre-vote is not granted.
Persistence: in every round that delivered the accepted message the follower must still not grant the retried pre-vote while the leader is alive; witnesses in rounds 1-3 are the violated case.

Repair is not broken: a round that starts without a leader context is restored to lead=1 by the leader's real heartbeat, so the repeated failure comes from the sender's cadence, not from a broken repair path.

investigations.question: Does a MsgForgetLeader that arrives from a peer through the documented inbound path (RawNode.Step / node.Step) reach the follower state machine and clear its live leader context, and does that change the support the follower gives a log-up-to-date candidate's pre-vote while the leader is still alive?
investigations.hypothesis: MsgForgetLeader is produced only locally (RawNode.ForgetLeader -> raft.Step), but the type is not listed in isLocalMsg, so the inbound filter that exists to drop locally-generated types does not drop it: a peer can deliver it with From=3 and no term field, it is treated as a local (term-0) message, stepFollower sets r.lead=None, and the follower then ignores the CheckQuorum lease check when answering a candidate's MsgPreVote at term+1.
investigations.discriminator: Deliver the identical real MsgPreVote from a real campaigning node 3 to follower 2 twice: once while 2 holds a lease from leader 1 (expect no response at all), and once after the inbound MsgForgetLeader from node 3 (expect MsgPreVoteResp with Reject=false). A competing explanation (node 2 grants pre-votes regardless of the lease) is excluded by the first delivery; a competing explanation (the general inbound filter is broken) is excluded by the MsgCheckQuorum control from the same sender.

gaps.question: How long does the window opened by one inbound MsgForgetLeader last in the target's own clock (until the next heartbeat or MsgApp from the live leader restores r.lead), and can a candidate in that window collect a full quorum of pre-vote grants and win an election while the incumbent leader is still serving?

investigations.question: Once one inbound MsgForgetLeader has cleared a follower's leader context, for how long does the lease suppression stay off in the target's own clock (measured as leader ticks until the next real heartbeat or MsgApp restores r.lead), and can forged deliveries to a quorum of followers produce a second leader at a higher term while the incumbent leader is still serving?
investigations.hypothesis: The suppression stays off until the next genuine leader message is processed (stepFollower sets r.lead=m.From on MsgApp/MsgHeartbeat/MsgSnap), i.e. up to one heartbeat interval per follower; because each follower accepts the forged message independently, delivering it to a quorum lets an up-to-date candidate collect enough pre-votes and then votes to become leader at a higher term, while the incumbent leader still reports leadership.
investigations.discriminator: Extend the executed scenario with (a) the leader's next real heartbeat after the forged message, measuring in ticks when lead returns to 1 and whether a further pre-vote is ignored again, and (b) a three-voter group in which the forged message is delivered to two followers before a real campaign, observing the voters' pre-vote/vote responses and the resulting soft state of both the candidate and the incumbent leader.

investigations.question: After the forged path has produced a second leader at a higher term, does the incumbent step down correctly when the new leader's MsgApp/MsgHeartbeat arrive, and does the new leader's log contain every entry committed under the incumbent (no divergence or lost commitment), so the harm is bounded to the unnecessary leadership change rather than log-integrity loss?
investigations.hypothesis: Delivering the new leader's term-3 MsgApp to node 1 makes it become a follower at term 3 (stepFollower sets lead=1 and handleAppendEntries matches at (index=11, term=2)), so the incumbent's authority is shed by the ordinary higher-term rule, while the new leader's log already contains the entries committed under the incumbent.
investigations.discriminator: Extend group B by feeding node 3's post-election MsgApp and heartbeats to node 1 and observing node 1's soft state and the new leader's log prefix; a clean transfer with the committed prefix intact bounds the defect to disruption, whereas any index/term mismatch or entry loss would widen it to a safety defect.

scope.description: Three real RawNode instances (ids 1,2,3) sharing a snapshot at index=10/term=1 with ConfState voters {1,2,3}, all with CheckQuorum=true and PreVote=true. Real producers are used throughout: node 1 wins a real election through delivered MsgVote/MsgVoteResp and replicates its term-2 entry; node 1's heartbeat is produced by a logical tick and delivered to node 2; node 3's MsgPreVote is produced by a real Campaign. The only constructed message is the inbound MsgForgetLeader in peer wire form (From=3, To=2, no term field), delivered through the documented public inbound path RawNode.Step.
assumptions: A peer may deliver a protobuf message of any MessageType to this node's public inbound path; raft's wire format carries no sender authentication, so the target's own IsLocalMsg filter is the only guard for locally-generated types.
Ticks are the target's logical clock; node 2 is not ticked between the heartbeat and the pre-vote deliveries, so its election-timer lease is active (electionElapsed=0, electionTimeout=10).
The pre-vote request is generated by a real campaigning node whose log equals node 2's log, so isUpToDate holds and the lease test is the only reason to withhold support.
excluded: Winning an election: no MsgPreVoteResp is delivered back to node 3, so the experiment measures node 2's response, not a completed election.
Transport-level authentication or rafthttp behaviour, which is outside this module.

basis.prefix: Build three real RawNode instances from MemoryStorage snapshots (index=10, term=1, voters {1,2,3}) with CheckQuorum+PreVote, run a real election for node 1, replicate its term-2 entry, tick the leader once to emit a real heartbeat and deliver it to node 2 (and to node 3 silently), then (a) deliver MsgCheckQuorum from node 3 to node 2 as the local-type control, (b) deliver node 3's real MsgPreVote to node 2 and observe whether any MsgPreVoteResp is produced, (c) deliver the peer-form MsgForgetLeader (From=3, To=2, no term) to node 2 through RawNode.Step, and (d) deliver the identical MsgPreVote again. Readiness is observed through the public Ready()/Advance() contract and leader context through BasicStatus().SoftState.Lead; every event below is emitted as a CA_EVENT JSON line.
basis.responsibility: The application must deliver inbound peer messages to RawNode.Step/node.Step; the raft module owns the decision which message types are acceptable from the network (isLocalMsg) and owns the meaning of MsgForgetLeader as a local authority-state change.

assertion.value: raft: cannot step raft local message

comparisons.description: Control: a message type that is classified as local, delivered through the same inbound path from the same peer, is rejected by the filter and leaves the leader context unchanged.
Control: while the follower holds a lease from the live leader, the identical pre-vote request from an up-to-date candidate is not granted (the request is ignored without a response).
The defect predicate: a peer-supplied MsgForgetLeader is not accepted by the inbound path (accepted=false would mean the filter rejected it).

Consequence: if the inbound MsgForgetLeader was accepted, the follower must still not grant the identical pre-vote request while the leader is alive; a witness with forget_accepted=true and granted=true is the violated case.
Independent control: the same state change is produced by the local API for a follower that still considers the leader live (lead 1 -> 0), which is why the network path must not reach it.

scope.description: Two real three-voter RawNode groups in one process (voters {1,2,3}, CheckQuorum+PreVote, shared storage snapshot at index=10/term=1). Group A repeats the executed scenario (real election for node 1, real heartbeat tick, local-type control, real MsgPreVote from a real campaign, peer-form MsgForgetLeader, re-delivery of the identical pre-vote) and then advances the leader's logical clock by one tick so that its next real heartbeat repairs follower 2. Group B does the same until the pre-vote control, then forges the same message to the quorum-relevant follower and lets node 3's campaign complete with the grants actually produced, observing pre-vote, vote and leadership outcomes.
assumptions: A peer may deliver an arbitrary protobuf message type to the public inbound path RawNode.Step; raft's wire form is unauthenticated, so the module's own IsLocalMsg filter is the boundary in scope.

Ticks are the target's logical clock: leader ticks of 1 with HeartbeatTick=1 produce one heartbeat per tick, and no follower is ticked between measurements, so the follower's own election timeout never fires during the run.

In group B the same node (3) both delivers the forged message and campaigns; the shared node identity is used only to correlate the admission event with the result event, so the experiment does not claim that attacker and candidate must coincide.
Grants are returned to the candidate through the same public Step path; the incumbent leader is not fed the new leader's messages, so its own demotion is outside this bounded prefix.
excluded: Transport authentication and rafthttp behaviour, outside this module.
Whether the deposed leader eventually steps down once the new leader's messages reach it (not delivered here).

basis.prefix: Build six real RawNode instances as two independent three-voter groups from MemoryStorage snapshots (index=10, term=1, voters {1,2,3}) with CheckQuorum+PreVote; run a real election for node 1 and replicate its term-2 entry in each group; tick the leader once and deliver the real heartbeat to each follower. Group A: deliver MsgCheckQuorum from node 3 (local-type control), deliver node 3's real MsgPreVote (under-lease control), deliver the peer-form MsgForgetLeader (From=3, To=2, no term), re-deliver the identical pre-vote, then tick the leader once more, deliver the next real heartbeat and re-deliver the pre-vote a third time. Group B: deliver the real MsgPreVote (control), forge the same message to node 2, re-deliver the pre-vote and feed its grant back to node 3, deliver node 3's resulting MsgVote to node 2 and feed its grant back, and record both nodes' leadership state. All observations come from the public Step/Ready/Advance contract and BasicStatus; each event is a CA_EVENT JSON line.
basis.responsibility: The application must deliver inbound peer messages to RawNode.Step; the raft module owns which message types are acceptable from the network and owns the meaning of MsgForgetLeader as a local authority-state change, and it owns the lease rule that is supposed to keep followers from supporting a candidate while the leader is alive.

assertion.value: raft: cannot step raft local message

comparisons.description: Control: a genuinely local type from the same peer is still rejected by the inbound filter.
Control: the pre-vote is not granted while the lease holds.
Defect predicate: the peer-form MsgForgetLeader must not be accepted by the inbound path.
Consequence: if the message was accepted, the follower must still not grant the identical pre-vote while the leader is alive.
Re-specified control: the same state change is produced by the local API on a follower with a live leader context (lead 1 -> 0), which is why the network path must not reach it.
Repair path: the leader's next real heartbeat (one leader tick with HeartbeatTick=1) restores the follower's leader context.
Window bound: once the leader context is restored, the identical pre-vote is ignored again, so the window opened by the forged message is closed by the next leader message.
Group B control: the quorum-relevant follower does not grant the pre-vote while the lease holds.
Group B defect predicate: the peer-form MsgForgetLeader is not accepted by the inbound path.
Group B consequence (pre-vote): after the accepted forgery the same request is granted.
Group B consequence (vote): the follower that was made to forget also grants the real vote that lets the candidate reach a quorum.
Group B disruption: an up-to-date candidate must not become leader at a higher term while the incumbent leader is still serving; a witness where node 3 is StateLeader is the violated case.

experiments.revision_reason: Adds the repair-path measurement (one further leader tick -> next real heartbeat -> lead restored -> a third identical pre-vote ignored again), re-specifies the local-API control with a heartbeat prerequisite that carries the same identity field as its result (the previous version was unknown because the heartbeat event had no 'node' field), and adds a second test function in which the forged message reaches the quorum-relevant follower before a real campaign, so the election consequence is observed. scope.description: Third test function in the same harness file: a real three-voter group is elected for node 1, the peer-form MsgForgetLeader is delivered to the quorum-relevant follower, a real campaign by node 3 is completed with the grants actually produced (pre-vote, vote), and then the new leader's first append is delivered to the deposed incumbent through the public Step path, observing the incumbent's soft state, the append's anchor, and the acknowledgement.
assumptions: A peer may deliver an arbitrary protobuf message type to the public inbound path RawNode.Step.

All three nodes start from the same storage snapshot (index=10, term=1, voters {1,2,3}); in this harness the followers never receive leader 1's term-2 entry, so the incumbent's committed prefix is (index=10, term=1) and its term-2 entry stays uncommitted.
The incumbent is not fed anything until the new leader's append, so its demotion is measured against that single append; the new leader's own commit value is emitted but not compared.
excluded: Any claim about the new leader's commit index: its operands (per-peer Match) are not fully observed through the public API here.

result.summary: Registered the next judgment-changing question and requested its experiment: whether a peer that re-delivers the same peer-form MsgForgetLeader once per heartbeat round keeps a healthy leader's follower from enforcing its lease, so the identical up-to-date candidate's pre-vote is granted every round instead of within a single heartbeat interval. New child question @forged_forget_persistence plus a fresh fixed experiment (fourth test function in the same harness, its own p_ stream): the control round without the forgery, three rounds each delivering the leader's real heartbeat, the same forged message and the same retried pre-vote, and a comparison that checks the repair path still restores lead=1 each round so a repeated failure would be attributed to the sender's cadence rather than a broken repair. The harness runs natively with the predicted events (round 0 no grant; rounds 1-3 restore, lose, and grant while the leader stays StateLeader at term 2), and validation passed with the execution requested. Incomplete: the receipt and its interpretation are pending, so the persistence claim is not yet part of the current account.

investigations.question: Does a MsgForgetLeader that arrives from a peer through the documented inbound path (RawNode.Step / node.Step) reach the follower state machine and clear its live leader context, and does that change the support the follower gives a log-up-to-date candidate's pre-vote while the leader is still alive?
investigations.hypothesis: MsgForgetLeader is produced only locally (RawNode.ForgetLeader -> raft.Step), but the type is not listed in isLocalMsg, so the inbound filter that exists to drop locally-generated types does not drop it: a peer can deliver it with From=3 and no term field, it is treated as a local (term-0) message, stepFollower sets r.lead=None, and the follower then ignores the CheckQuorum lease check when answering a candidate's MsgPreVote at term+1.
investigations.discriminator: Deliver the identical real MsgPreVote from a real campaigning node 3 to follower 2 twice: once while 2 holds a lease from leader 1 (expect no response at all), and once after the inbound MsgForgetLeader from node 3 (expect MsgPreVoteResp with Reject=false). A competing explanation (node 2 grants pre-votes regardless of the lease) is excluded by the first delivery; a competing explanation (the general inbound filter is broken) is excluded by the MsgCheckQuorum control from the same sender.

gaps.question: How long does the window opened by one inbound MsgForgetLeader last in the target's own clock (until the next heartbeat or MsgApp from the live leader restores r.lead), and can a candidate in that window collect a full quorum of pre-vote grants and win an election while the incumbent leader is still serving?

investigations.question: Once one inbound MsgForgetLeader has cleared a follower's leader context, for how long does the lease suppression stay off in the target's own clock (measured as leader ticks until the next real heartbeat or MsgApp restores r.lead), and can forged deliveries to a quorum of followers produce a second leader at a higher term while the incumbent leader is still serving?
investigations.hypothesis: The suppression stays off until the next genuine leader message is processed (stepFollower sets r.lead=m.From on MsgApp/MsgHeartbeat/MsgSnap), i.e. up to one heartbeat interval per follower; because each follower accepts the forged message independently, delivering it to a quorum lets an up-to-date candidate collect enough pre-votes and then votes to become leader at a higher term, while the incumbent leader still reports leadership.
investigations.discriminator: Extend the executed scenario with (a) the leader's next real heartbeat after the forged message, measuring in ticks when lead returns to 1 and whether a further pre-vote is ignored again, and (b) a three-voter group in which the forged message is delivered to two followers before a real campaign, observing the voters' pre-vote/vote responses and the resulting soft state of both the candidate and the incumbent leader.

investigations.question: After the forged path has produced a second leader at a higher term, does the incumbent step down correctly when the new leader's MsgApp/MsgHeartbeat arrive, and does the new leader's log contain every entry committed under the incumbent (no divergence or lost commitment), so the harm is bounded to the unnecessary leadership change rather than log-integrity loss?
investigations.hypothesis: Delivering the new leader's term-3 MsgApp to node 1 makes it become a follower at term 3 (stepFollower sets lead=1 and handleAppendEntries matches at (index=11, term=2)), so the incumbent's authority is shed by the ordinary higher-term rule, while the new leader's log already contains the entries committed under the incumbent.
investigations.discriminator: Extend group B by feeding node 3's post-election MsgApp and heartbeats to node 1 and observing node 1's soft state and the new leader's log prefix; a clean transfer with the committed prefix intact bounds the defect to disruption, whereas any index/term mismatch or entry loss would widen it to a safety defect.

investigations.question: Does a peer that re-delivers the same MsgForgetLeader once per heartbeat round keep a follower from enforcing its leader lease while the leader is healthy, so that the identical up-to-date candidate's pre-vote is granted on every attempt rather than during a single heartbeat interval?
investigations.hypothesis: Each round follows the same path: the leader's real heartbeat restores r.lead (=1), the accepted peer-form MsgForgetLeader clears it again (=0), and with lead==None the CheckQuorum lease test fails, so the up-to-date candidate's pre-vote is granted every round; the repair path is genuinely working (lead returns to 1 each round) but is defeated by the attacker's cadence rather than being broken.
investigations.discriminator: Round 0 without any forgery (control: no grant), then rounds 1-3 each delivering the leader's real heartbeat, the same forged message and the same retried pre-vote. A single grant would bound the effect to one window; grants in every round while the leader keeps beating and stays leader show that the window can be kept open indefinitely by the sender.

scope.description: Three real RawNode instances (ids 1,2,3) sharing a snapshot at index=10/term=1 with ConfState voters {1,2,3}, all with CheckQuorum=true and PreVote=true. Real producers are used throughout: node 1 wins a real election through delivered MsgVote/MsgVoteResp and replicates its term-2 entry; node 1's heartbeat is produced by a logical tick and delivered to node 2; node 3's MsgPreVote is produced by a real Campaign. The only constructed message is the inbound MsgForgetLeader in peer wire form (From=3, To=2, no term field), delivered through the documented public inbound path RawNode.Step.
assumptions: A peer may deliver a protobuf message of any MessageType to this node's public inbound path; raft's wire format carries no sender authentication, so the target's own IsLocalMsg filter is the only guard for locally-generated types.
Ticks are the target's logical clock; node 2 is not ticked between the heartbeat and the pre-vote deliveries, so its election-timer lease is active (electionElapsed=0, electionTimeout=10).
The pre-vote request is generated by a real campaigning node whose log equals node 2's log, so isUpToDate holds and the lease test is the only reason to withhold support.
excluded: Winning an election: no MsgPreVoteResp is delivered back to node 3, so the experiment measures node 2's response, not a completed election.
Transport-level authentication or rafthttp behaviour, which is outside this module.

basis.prefix: Build three real RawNode instances from MemoryStorage snapshots (index=10, term=1, voters {1,2,3}) with CheckQuorum+PreVote, run a real election for node 1, replicate its term-2 entry, tick the leader once to emit a real heartbeat and deliver it to node 2 (and to node 3 silently), then (a) deliver MsgCheckQuorum from node 3 to node 2 as the local-type control, (b) deliver node 3's real MsgPreVote to node 2 and observe whether any MsgPreVoteResp is produced, (c) deliver the peer-form MsgForgetLeader (From=3, To=2, no term) to node 2 through RawNode.Step, and (d) deliver the identical MsgPreVote again. Readiness is observed through the public Ready()/Advance() contract and leader context through BasicStatus().SoftState.Lead; every event below is emitted as a CA_EVENT JSON line.
basis.responsibility: The application must deliver inbound peer messages to RawNode.Step/node.Step; the raft module owns the decision which message types are acceptable from the network (isLocalMsg) and owns the meaning of MsgForgetLeader as a local authority-state change.

assertion.value: raft: cannot step raft local message

comparisons.description: Control: a message type that is classified as local, delivered through the same inbound path from the same peer, is rejected by the filter and leaves the leader context unchanged.
Control: while the follower holds a lease from the live leader, the identical pre-vote request from an up-to-date candidate is not granted (the request is ignored without a response).
The defect predicate: a peer-supplied MsgForgetLeader is not accepted by the inbound path (accepted=false would mean the filter rejected it).

Consequence: if the inbound MsgForgetLeader was accepted, the follower must still not grant the identical pre-vote request while the leader is alive; a witness with forget_accepted=true and granted=true is the violated case.
Independent control: the same state change is produced by the local API for a follower that still considers the leader live (lead 1 -> 0), which is why the network path must not reach it.

scope.description: Two real three-voter RawNode groups in one process (voters {1,2,3}, CheckQuorum+PreVote, shared storage snapshot at index=10/term=1). Group A repeats the executed scenario (real election for node 1, real heartbeat tick, local-type control, real MsgPreVote from a real campaign, peer-form MsgForgetLeader, re-delivery of the identical pre-vote) and then advances the leader's logical clock by one tick so that its next real heartbeat repairs follower 2. Group B does the same until the pre-vote control, then forges the same message to the quorum-relevant follower and lets node 3's campaign complete with the grants actually produced, observing pre-vote, vote and leadership outcomes.
assumptions: A peer may deliver an arbitrary protobuf message type to the public inbound path RawNode.Step; raft's wire form is unauthenticated, so the module's own IsLocalMsg filter is the boundary in scope.

Ticks are the target's logical clock: leader ticks of 1 with HeartbeatTick=1 produce one heartbeat per tick, and no follower is ticked between measurements, so the follower's own election timeout never fires during the run.

In group B the same node (3) both delivers the forged message and campaigns; the shared node identity is used only to correlate the admission event with the result event, so the experiment does not claim that attacker and candidate must coincide.
Grants are returned to the candidate through the same public Step path; the incumbent leader is not fed the new leader's messages, so its own demotion is outside this bounded prefix.
excluded: Transport authentication and rafthttp behaviour, outside this module.
Whether the deposed leader eventually steps down once the new leader's messages reach it (not delivered here).

basis.prefix: Build six real RawNode instances as two independent three-voter groups from MemoryStorage snapshots (index=10, term=1, voters {1,2,3}) with CheckQuorum+PreVote; run a real election for node 1 and replicate its term-2 entry in each group; tick the leader once and deliver the real heartbeat to each follower. Group A: deliver MsgCheckQuorum from node 3 (local-type control), deliver node 3's real MsgPreVote (under-lease control), deliver the peer-form MsgForgetLeader (From=3, To=2, no term), re-deliver the identical pre-vote, then tick the leader once more, deliver the next real heartbeat and re-deliver the pre-vote a third time. Group B: deliver the real MsgPreVote (control), forge the same message to node 2, re-deliver the pre-vote and feed its grant back to node 3, deliver node 3's resulting MsgVote to node 2 and feed its grant back, and record both nodes' leadership state. Only the leader is ticked, so follower election timeouts never fire.
All nodes start from the same storage snapshot (index=10, term=1, voters {1,2,3}); the incumbent's committed prefix is (index=10, term=1) and its term-2 entry at index 11 stays uncommitted.
The new leader's own commit value is emitted as raw data only; no comparison depends on it.
excluded: Any claim about the new leader's commit index (per-peer Match is not fully observable through the public API here).

basis.prefix: Run all three TestAssurance functions. The third repeats the election, heartbeat, under-lease control, forged message, re-delivered pre-vote and vote, then takes the new leader's first MsgApp, delivers it to the deposed incumbent and emits the incumbent's post-append soft state with the append anchor (prev index/term), the appended entry, the acknowledgement and the incumbent's committed index before the append. Each campaign-request event now carries the identity field 'leader' so the admission can be correlated in both streams.
basis.responsibility: The raft module owns the higher-term authority rule that a node sheds leadership when it learns a newer term, and owns whether the log it accepts continues the committed prefix it already had.

comparisons.description: Control: the quorum-relevant follower does not grant the pre-vote while its leader context is intact.
Defect predicate: the peer-form MsgForgetLeader must not be accepted through the inbound path.
Disruption: an up-to-date candidate must not take leadership at a higher term while the incumbent is still serving.
Bound: the deposed incumbent accepts the new leader's append and sheds leadership on the higher term rather than fighting it.
Bound: the new leader's anchor is exactly the incumbent's committed prefix (index 10, term 1), so no committed index is lost by the change.
Bound: after the append the deposed incumbent follows the new leader rather than remaining leaderless.

before.description: Third test function in the same harness file: a real three-voter group is elected for node 1, the peer-form MsgForgetLeader is delivered to the quorum-relevant follower, a real campaign by node 3 is completed with the grants actually produced (pre-vote, vote), and then the new leader's first append is delivered to the deposed incumbent through the public Step path, observing the incumbent's soft state, the append's anchor, and the acknowledgement.
assumptions: A peer may deliver an arbitrary protobuf message type to the public inbound path RawNode.Step.
Ticks are the target's logical clock; only the leader is ticked, so follower election timeouts never fire.

All three nodes start from the same storage snapshot (index=10, term=1, voters {1,2,3}); in this harness the followers never receive leader 1's term-2 entry, so the incumbent's committed prefix is (index=10, term=1) and its term-2 entry stays uncommitted.
The incumbent is not fed anything until the new leader's append, so its demotion is measured against that single append; the new leader's own commit value is emitted but not compared.
excluded: Any claim about the new leader's commit index: its operands (per-peer Match) are not fully observed through the public API here.

experiments.revision_reason: The aftermath stream (third test function) now emits its own event names (a_heartbeat_delivered, a_prevote_outcome, a_prevote_request, a_inbound_forget_leader, a_vote_outcome, a_leadership_state) instead of reusing the quorum stream's names, and the comparisons for this experiment bind to prerequisites derived from those names. This removes the only remaining harness-side gap: previously the admission check could pick the quorum stream's campaign admission and then find no result in that stream, which left the three bound comparisons unknown in both earlier receipts. Same scenario, same nodes, same six comparisons otherwise.

scope.description: Fourth test function in the same harness file: a real three-voter group elected for node 1, a real pre-vote request produced by a real campaign on node 3 and retried unchanged, and a loop of three rounds in which the leader is ticked, its real heartbeat is delivered to follower 2, the peer-form MsgForgetLeader (From=3, To=2, no term field) is delivered through RawNode.Step, and the retried pre-vote is delivered again.
assumptions: A peer may deliver an arbitrary protobuf message type to the public inbound path RawNode.Step, repeatedly and at will.
Ticks are the target's logical clock; only the leader is ticked, so follower election timeouts never fire and the leader stays healthy throughout.
The candidate's request is reused unchanged across rounds, representing a retry by a candidate that is still waiting; the follower stays at term 2 because a pre-vote never changes the term.
All nodes start from equal storage snapshots (index=10, term=1, voters {1,2,3}).
excluded: Wall-clock timing and multi-host transport behaviour.
Whether a real candidate would keep retrying after its first grant is taken (the grant is fed nowhere here).

basis.prefix: Elect node 1 for real, deliver its real heartbeat to follower 2, emit the pre-vote control round, then repeat three rounds: leader tick (one heartbeat), deliver the real heartbeat to follower 2, deliver the peer-form MsgForgetLeader, deliver the unchanged retried pre-vote. Each round emits the heartbeat's lead transition, the accepted message with its lead transition, and the pre-vote outcome (whether a MsgPreVoteResp was produced and whether it rejected).
basis.responsibility: The raft module owns the lease rule that keeps a follower from supporting a candidate while it hears from a live leader, and owns which message types are acceptable from the network.

comparisons.description: Control: in the round without any forged message the retried pre-vote is not granted.
Persistence: in every round that delivered the accepted message the follower must still not grant the retried pre-vote while the leader is alive; witnesses in rounds 1-3 are the violated case.

Repair is not broken: a round that starts without a leader context is restored to lead=1 by the leader's real heartbeat, so the repeated failure comes from the sender's cadence, not from a broken repair path.
